correctness.rationale: Unitary discrete Fourier transforms on rings with 2j+1 samples create an upper triangular system ordered by absolute azimuth m. Diagonal m-block rows j>=|m| contain associated-Legendre radial values, and derivative polynomials of degrees 0,..,L-|m|-1 give ordinary Vandermonde determinants. Multiplying all signed-m blocks yields C_L times (1-x_j²)^{j(j+1)} and |x_j-x_i|^{2(2i+1)}, independent of ring offsets. Distinct interior heights make every factor nonzero. Taking log, its Hessian quadratic form is the sum of negative pole diagonal curvatures and negative pairwise squared-difference penalties; it is negative definite on each of the (L-1)! convex ordering chambers. Pole or collision boundaries force log determinant to -infinity, hence one interior nondegenerate maximizer per chamber. Independently verified C2=729/(1024*pi^4), C3=5189853515625/(1073741824*pi^9), L3 Hessian curvature, and compared analytical factorization with published nine-node L3 formula. These finite checks support but do not prove all L. No global best permutation, stability or condition number is claimed.
